    POS Cashier System

    Point of Sale (POS) Cashier Website

    Speeding up checkout & inventory tracking for MSMEs with an efficiency-first UI.

    Buka Proyek (GitHub)
    terminal · ~/projects/pos-cashier

    ~/projects/pos-cashier $ glow README.md

    Why It Was Built

    Designed to address manual transaction challenges faced by MSMEs and small retail businesses:

    • Speed up the checkout transaction process to under 10 seconds.
    • Minimize human errors in total bill and change calculations.
    • Automate inventory tracking and daily transaction logging in real-time.

    Key Features

    • Authentication & Role Management: Distinct access rights and login screens for cashiers and administrators.
    • Point of Sale (POS) Interface: Fast product search, quantity input, and automated total and change calculation.
    • Inventory Management (CRUD): Ability to add, edit, and delete product details, prices, and stock counts.
    • Transaction History & Receipts: Transaction logging with options to print digital or physical receipts.
    • Responsive Layout: Optimized interface for laptops, tablets, and touchscreen POS terminals.

    Tech Stack

    • UI/UX Design: Figma (Wireframing, High-Fidelity Design, Interactive Prototyping)
    • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS / Bootstrap
    • Backend & Database: Node.js / PHP / Laravel & MySQL

    Architectural & Design Decisions

    • Efficiency-First UI: Large touch and click targets for numbers and products to speed up cashier navigation without relying heavily on a mouse.
    • Minimal Steps to Checkout: Streamlined flow from product selection to receipt printing.
    • Design System: Applied Atomic Design principles in Figma for buttons, product cards, and tables.

    Bandsy

    Bandsy

    IELTS Academic prep across all four modules, graded by a model you choose.

    Buka Proyek (GitHub)
    terminal · ~/projects/bandsy

    ~/projects/bandsy $ glow README.md

    Why I built it

    I had to take IELTS and had no idea where to start. The practice tests were all over the place, spread across 24 Cambridge books, and I was honestly overwhelmed.

    So I built one place to take me through it end to end, with AI doing the parts that usually need a tutor: marking my Writing and examining my Speaking.

    What it does

    • Reading and Listening look like the computer-delivered exam, with the real book audio, played once in a mock.
    • Explain on any answer quotes where it is in the passage or transcript, why the key is right and why yours didn't fit.
    • Writing is graded on the four criteria with errors marked inline. Speaking is a three-part test with a spoken examiner.
    • One suggested session a day, weighted to your weakest module.

    How it's built

    • A pipeline turned the book PDFs and audio into tests: OCR, answer keys, transcripts repaired against the recordings with local Whisper, and validators for every 40 of 40 answers.
    • Speech-to-text and the examiner's voice run locally, with faster-whisper and Kokoro.
    • Answers are marked the IELTS way: alternatives, optional words, pairs in either order.

    Decisions worth noting

    • A model is used in the pipeline only where OCR can't do the job.
    • Explanations are cached per question and answer, so a second click costs nothing.
    • A job without a chosen model refuses to run rather than picking one for you.

    Mentora

    Mentora

    A local-first AI tutor that teaches anything and everything code.

    Buka Proyek (GitHub)
    terminal · ~/projects/mentora

    ~/projects/mentora $ glow README.md

    Why I built it

    AI fatigue. So much of my thinking had been handed to a model that I wanted to start from scratch and build myself back up. No more third party thinking.

    So I used AI to beat AI: a tutor on a fixed path from TypeScript to agents, where I write the code and it notices what I keep getting wrong.

    What it does

    • A thirteen phase curriculum, about 976 hours at eighteen a week, from TypeScript and algorithms through full stack, machine learning and agents to interview practice.
    • The tutor adapts the pacing, never the content.
    • Exercises run in the browser in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python or Java, with daily spaced reviews and mistakes tracked so a weak spot gets drilled.

    How it's built

    • The tutor runs on Claude through a Claude Code login, with Ollama as the fallback.
    • Every exercise's tests pass on its reference solution and fail on its starter, checked in every language it has.
    • Progress lives in one SQLite file on your machine, with a backup export.

    Decisions worth noting

    • The curriculum is a fixed map, changed only as a deliberate, versioned decision.
    • The machine learning phases were planned against real syllabi: Stanford CS229, CS231n and CS224n, MIT 6.S191 and fast.ai.

    "dependencies": ["Next.js", "TypeScript", "SQLite", "Claude Code", "Ollama"]

    About

    Hey! I'm Irbah's AI, the one that doesn't sleep. Ask me anything about his UI/UX design journey, tech stack, or projects, and if you want to reach him directly, check his phone on the desk.

    Hi! I'm a passionate UI/UX Designer dedicated to crafting intuitive and visually engaging digital experiences. I bridge the gap between aesthetics and functionality to create interfaces that feel smooth, natural, and enjoyable for users.

    My journey into design actually started unexpectedly during school assignments where I first played around with HTML and CSS. Building those early web projects sparked my curiosity—I realized how much I enjoyed shaping how things look and feel on a screen.

    Over time, that curiosity evolved into a deep passion for UI/UX design. Today, I focus on understanding user needs and turning ideas into clean, functional, and visually compelling designs. I'm constantly learning, experimenting, and growing as a designer with every new challenge.

    How It All Started
    My journey into the tech world officially kicked off when I chose to major in Software Engineering (RPL / Rekayasa Perangkat Lunak) in vocational high school. That was my very first introduction to the world of code, logic, and building digital products from scratch.

    Discovering My Passion for Design
    While working on various school assignments and building web projects using HTML and CSS, I noticed something interesting. I enjoyed the coding part, but what really got me excited was shaping how the website looked and how users interacted with it. I found myself spending hours perfecting layouts, choosing colors, and tweaking element alignments to make sure everything felt right.

    That realization led me straight into UI/UX Design. Having a background in RPL gave me a huge advantage—I don't just design pretty interfaces; I design with a clear understanding of how code works under the hood.

    Tech Stack: Figma, Tailwind CSS, React, HTML, CSS, Laravel, Nuxt, Java.
